chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Awf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The gatherings are with the confidentiality.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping secrets in a gathering?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the 'trust' (amana) of a gathering as a binding ethical obligation among attendees. This principle underscores the sanctity of private discourse in Shia social ethics, where confidentiality is not merely polite discretion but a religious duty, fostering trust and intimacy in communal interactions. The brevity of the text highlights its status as a foundational legal and moral maxim in fiqh al-ahwal (personal status law).
